[IMC 2013 Q4] A standard pack of pumpkin seeds contains 40 seeds. A special pack contains 25% more seeds. Rachel bought a special pack and 70% of the seeds germinated.

How many pumpkin plants did Rachel have?

subskill.name: Solve problems in context involving percentage changes and arithmetic operations, without a calculator.

questions.content:
[IMC 2013 Q5] The northern wheatear is a small bird weighing less than an ounce. Some northern wheatears migrate from sub-Saharan Africa to their Arctic breeding grounds, travelling almost 15 000 km. The journey takes just over 7 weeks.

Roughly how far do they travel each day, on average?

subskill.name: Estimate the result of a division by a decimal using rounding to significant figures.

questions.content: [IMC 2013 Q6] Which of the following has the least value?

subskill.name: Calculate an integer power of an integer which is possibly negative.

questions.content:
[IMC 2013 Q7] The faces of a regular octahedron are to be painted so that no two faces which have an edge in common are painted in the same colour.

What is the smallest number of colours required?

[IMC 2013 Q8] Jim rolled some dice and was surprised that the sum of the scores on the dice was equal to the product of the scores on the dice.

One of the dice showed a score of 2, one showed 3 and one showed 5. The rest showed a score of 1.

How many dice did Jim roll?
[IMC 2013 Q9] Jane has 20 identical cards in the shape of an isosceles right-angled triangle. She uses the cards to make the five shapes below. Which of the shapes has the shortest perimeter?

subskill.name: Use Pythagoras' theorem to find a cost or other physical quantity involving the perimeter of a shape.

questions.content:
[IMC 2013 Q10] [m]ABCDE[/m] is a regular pentagon and [m]BCF[/m] is an equilateral triangle such that [m]F[/m] is inside [m]ABCDE[/m].

What is the size of [m]\angle FAB[/m]?

subskill.name: Solve problems by use of case analysis.

questions.content: [IMC 2013 Q11] For which of the following numbers is the sum of all its factors not equal to a square number?

subskill.name: Identify square numbers.

questions.content:
[IMC 2013 Q12] The sum one + four = seventy
becomes correct if we replace each word by the number of letters in it to give [m]3+4=7[/m].

Using the same convention, which of these words could be substituted for [m]x[/m] to make the sum three + five [m]=x[/m] true?

subskill.name: Use listing strategies to find the number of combinations that result in a given property.

questions.content:
[IMC 2013 Q13] Four congruent isosceles trapeziums are placed so that their longer parallel sides form the diagonals of a square [m]PQRS[/m], as shown. The point [m]X[/m] divides [m]PQ[/m] in the ratio [m]3:1[/m].

What fraction of the square is shaded?
[IMC 2013 Q14] Which of the following has the greatest value?

[IMC 2013 Q15] I have a bag of coins. In it, one third of the coins are gold, one fifth of them are silver, two sevenths are bronze and the rest are copper. My bag can hold a maximum of 200 coins.

How many coins are in my bag?

subskill.name: Determine the total of a physical quantity where costs or weights are assigned to each group.

questions.content: [IMC 2013 Q16] Which diagram shows the graph of [m]y=x[/m] after it has been rotated [m]90^{\circ}[/m] clockwise about the point [m]\left(1,1\right)[/m]?

[IMC 2013 Q17] The diagram shows four equal discs and a square. Each disc touches its two neighbouring discs. Each corner of the square is positioned at the centre of a disc. The side length of the square is [m]2\div\pi[/m].

What is the length of the perimeter of the figure?

[IMC 2013 Q18] The triangle [m]T[/m] has sides of length 6, 5, 5. The triangle [m]U[/m] has sides of length 8, 5, 5.

What is the ratio area [m]T[/m] : area [m]U[/m]? Give your ratio in its simplest form.

[IMC 2013 Q19] Which of the expressions below is equivalent to:

[m]\left(x\div\left(y\div z\right)\right)\div\left(\left(x\div y\right)\div z\right)[/m]

[IMC 2013 Q20] Jack’s teacher asked him to draw a triangle of area 7cm2. Two sides are to be of length 6cm and 8cm.

How many possibilities are there for the length of the third side of the triangle?

[IMC 2013 Q21] The square [m]ABCD[/m] has an area of 196. It contains two overlapping squares; the larger of these squares has an area 4 times that of the smaller and the area of their overlap is 1. What is the total area of the shaded regions?

[IMC 2013 Q22] The diagrams show square placed inside two identical semicircles. In the lower diagram the two squares are identical.

What is the ratio of the areas of the two shaded regions? Give your ratio in its simplest form.

subskill.name: Form and solve a quadratic equation using the sides of a right-angled triangle using Pythagoras' Theorem.

questions.content:
[IMC 2013 Q23] Four brothers are discussing the order in which they were born. Two are lying and two are telling the truth. Which two are telling the truth?

Alfred: “Bernard is the youngest.”
Horatio: “Bernard is the oldest and I am the youngest.”
Inigo: “I was born last.”
Bernard: “I’m neither the youngest nor the oldest.”

[IMC 2013 Q24] The diagram shows a shaded shape bounded by circular arcs with the same radius. The centres of three arcs are the vertices of an equilateral triangle; the other three centres are the midpoints of the sides of the triangle. The sides of the triangle have length 2.

What is the difference between the area of the shaded shape and the area of the triangle? Give your area as an exact answer.

[IMC 2013 Q25] In 1984 the engineer and prolific prime-finder Harvey Dubner found the biggest known prime each of whose digits is either a one or a zero. The prime can be expressed as:

[m]\frac{10^{641}\times\left(10^{640}-1\right)}{9}+1[/m]

How many digits does this prime have?

[IMC 2010 Q2] Three of the interior angles of a given quadrilateral are each [m]80^{\circ}[/m].

What is the fourth angle of this quadrilateral?

subskill.name: Determine an angle in a quadrilateral given its other angles.

subskill.name: Know if a number is divisible by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 or 10.

[IMC 2010 Q4] A radio advertisement claimed that using a particular brand of artificial sweetener every day would ‘save 7 000 calories in a year’.

Approximately how many calories is this per day?

subskill.name: Estimate a value from a problem in context with a single arithmetic operation.

questions.content: [IMC 2010 Q5] Which of the following has the greatest value?

subskill.name: Multiply a fraction by a fraction, requiring simplification.

questions.content:
[IMC 2010 Q6] In triangle [m]PQR[/m], [m]S[/m] is a point on [m]QR[/m] such that 
[m]QS=SP=PR[/m] and [m]\angle QPS=20^{\circ}[/m]. What is the size of [m]\angle PRS[/m]?

subskill.name: Determine an angle using multiple angle laws in a diagram that involves an isosceles triangle.

questions.content:
[IMC 2010 Q7] The Three Choirs Festival is held annually. Its venue rotates in a three-year cycle among Hereford, Gloucester and Worcester. In 2009, it was held in Hereford, in 2010 it will be held in Gloucester, next year it will be held in Worcester.

Assuming that this three-year cycle continues, in which one of the following years will the Festival not be held in Worcester?
[IMC 2010 Q8] On a clock’s display, the time has just changed to 02:31. How many minutes will it be until all the digits 0, 1, 2, 3 next appear together again?

[IMC 2010 Q9] The perimeters of the three shapes shown are made up of straight lines and semi-circular arcs of diameter 2. They will fit snugly together as in a jigsaw.

What is the difference between the total perimeter of the three separate pieces and the perimeter of the shape formed when the three pieces fit together? Give your answer in terms of [m]\pi[/m].

subskill.name: Determine the perimeter of a shape where a semicircle is cut from a rectangle.

questions.content:
[IMC 2010 Q10] One year in the 1990s, January 1st fell on a Monday.

Eleven years later, January 1st was also a Monday. How many times did February 29th occur during those eleven years?

subskill.name: Know and use basic equivalences of time.

questions.content:
[IMC 2010 Q11] “You eat more than I do,” said Tweedledee to Tweedledum.
“That is not true,” said Tweedledum to Tweedledee.
“You are both wrong,” said Alice, to them both.
“You are right,” said the White Rabbit to Alice.

How many of the four statements were true?
[IMC 2010 Q12] A cuboid is cut away from a cube of side 10 cm as shown. By what fraction does the surface area of the solid decrease as a result?

[IMC 2010 Q13] At Corbett’s Ironmongery a fork handle and a candle cost a total of £6.10. The fork handle costs £4.60 more than the candle.

What is the cost of two fork handles and four candles?

subskill.name: Form and solve linear simultaneous equations/systems of equations for a given non-geometric context.

questions.content: [IMC 2010 Q14] Given that [m]4x-y=5[/m], [m]4y-z=7[/m] and [m]4z-x=18[/m], what is the value of [m]x+y+z[/m]?

[IMC 2010 Q15] Bill is trying to sketch the graph of [m]y=2x+6[/m] but in drawing the axes he has placed the [m]x[/m]-axis up the page and the [m]y[/m]-axis across the page.

Which of these five graphs is a correct sketch of [m]y=2x+6[/m] when the axes are placed in this way?

[IMC 2010 Q16] Albert Einstein is experimenting with two unusual clocks which both have 24-hour displays. One clock goes at twice the normal speed. The other clock goes backwards, but at the normal speed. Both clocks show the correct time at 13:00.

What is the correct time when the displays on the blocks next agree?

[IMC 2010 Q17] Last year Gill’s cylindrical 21st birthday cake wasn’t big enough to feed all her friends. This year she will double the radius and triple the height.

What will be the ratio of the volume of this year’s birthday cake to the volume of last year’s cake? Leave your ratio in its simplest form.

[IMC 2010 Q18] Supergran walks from her chalet to the top of the mountain. She knows that if she walks at a speed of 6 mph she will arrive at 1pm, whereas if she leaves at the same time and walks at 10 mph, she will arrive at 11am.

At what speed should she walk if she wants to arrive at 12 noon?

[IMC 2010 Q19] A snail is at one corner of the top face of a cube with side length 1 m. The snail can crawl at a speed of 1 m per hour.

What proportion of the cube’s surface is made up of points which the snail could reach within one hour?

[IMC 2010 Q20]

Shahbaz thinks of an integer, [m]n[/m], such that the difference between [m]\sqrt{n}[/m] and 7 is less than 1.

How many different possibilities are there for [m]n[/m]?

[IMC 2010 Q21] A square maze has 9 rooms with gaps in the walls between them. Once a person has travelled through a gap in the wall it then closes behind them.

How many different ways can someone travel through the maze from [m]X[/m] to [m]Y[/m]?

[IMC 2010 Q22] Curly and Larry like to have their orange squash made to the same strength. Unfortunately, Moe has put 25ml of squash with 175ml of water in Curly’s glass and 15ml of squash with 185ml of water in Larry’s glass.

How many millilitres of the mixture in Curly’s glass must be put into Larry’s glass so that they end up with drinks of the same strength?

[IMC 2010 Q23] The diagram shows a pattern of eight equal shaded squares inside a circle of area [m]\pi[/m] square units.

What is the area (in square units) of the shaded region? Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.

[IMC 2010 Q24] A new taxi firm needs a memorable phone number. They want a number which has a maximum of two different digits. Their phone number must start with the digit 3 and be six digits long.

How many such numbers are possible?

subskill.name: Determine the number of combinations when an item is repeatedly taken from the same group, but with replacement.

questions.content:
[IMC 2010 Q25] Two squares, each of side length [m]1+\sqrt{2}[/m] units, overlap. The overlapping region is a regular octagon.

What is the area (in square units) of the octagon?

[IMC 2015 Q20] A voucher code is made up of four characters. The first is a letter: [m]V[/m], [m]X[/m] or [m]P[/m]. The second and third are different digits. The fourth is the units digit of the sum of the second and third digits.

How many different voucher codes like this are there?

[IMC 2015 Q21] A rectangle is placed obliquely on top of an identical rectangle, as shown. The area of the overlapping region [m]X[/m] (shaded more darkly) is one eighth of the total shaded area.

What fraction of the area of one rectangle is [m]X[/m]?
[IMC 2015 Q22] The diagram shows a shaded region inside a large square. The shaded region is divided into small squares. What fraction of the area of the large square is shaded?

[IMC 2015 Q24] In square [m]RSTU[/m] a quarter-circle arc with centre [m]S[/m] is drawn from [m]T[/m] to [m]R[/m]. A point [m]P[/m] on this arc is 1 unit from [m]TU[/m] and 8 units from [m]RU[/m].

What is the length of the side of square [m]RSTU[/m]?
[IMC 2015 Q25] A point is marked one quarter of the way along each side of a triangle, as shown.  What fraction of the area of the triangle is shaded?

questions.content:
[IMC 2014 Q1] What is [m]25\%[/m] of [m]\frac{3}{4}[/m]?

(Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form)

subskill.name: Multiply a fraction by a fraction, requiring simplification.

questions.content:
[IMC 2014 Q2] Which is the smallest positive integer for which all these are true?

(i) It is odd.
(ii) It is not prime.
(iii) The next largest odd integer is not prime.

[IMC 2014 Q3] An equilateral triangle is placed inside a larger equilateral triangle so that the diagram has three lines of symmetry.

What is the value of [m]x[/m]?
[IMC 2014 Q4] You are given that [m]m[/m] is an even integer and [m]n[/m] is a odd integer. Which of these is an odd integer?

[IMC 2014 Q5] A ship’s bell is struck every half hour, starting with one bell at 0030, two bells (meaning the bell is struck twice) at 0100, three bells at 0130 until the cycle is complete with eight bells at 0400.

The cycle then starts again with one bell at 0430, two bells at 0500 and so on.

What is the total number of times the bell is struck between 0015 on one day and 0015 on the following day?

subskill.name: Use listing strategies to find the number of combinations that result in a given property.

questions.content:
[IMC 2014 Q6] The shape shown on the right was assembled from three identical copies of one of the smaller shapes below, without gaps or overlaps.

What smaller shape was used?

[IMC 2014 Q7] Just one positive integer (whole number) has exactly 8 factors including 6 and 15.

What is the integer?

subskill.name: List all factors of a number.

questions.content:
[IMC 2014 Q8] A large cube is made by stacking eight dice. The diagram shows the result, except that one of the dice is missing. Each die has faces with 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 pips and the total number of pips on each pair of opposite faces is 7. When two dice are placed face to face, the matching faces must have the same number of pips.

What could the missing die look like?

[IMC 2014 Q9] At the age of twenty-six, Gill has passed her driving test and bought a car. Her car uses [m]p[/m] litres of petrol per 100 km travelled.

How many litres of petrol would be required for a journey of [m]d[/m] km?

subskill.name: Write an expression or formula for a total quantity or cost involving two variables.

questions.content:
[IMC 2014 Q10] The diagram shows five touching semicircles, each with radius 2.

What is the length of the perimeter of the shaded shape?
Give your answer in terms of [m]\pi[/m].

[IMC 2014 Q11] Not all characters in the Woodentops series tell the truth. When Mr Plod asked them, “How many people are there in the Woodentops family?”, four of them replied as follows:

Jenny: “An even number.”
Willie: “An odd number.”
Sam: “A prime number.”
Mrs Scrubitt: “A number which is the product of two integers greater than one.”

How many of these four were telling the truth?

[IMC 2014 Q12] The diagram shows an isosceles right-angled triangle divided into strips of equal width. Four of the strips are shaded.

What fraction of the area of the triangle is shaded?
[IMC 2014 Q13] How many numbers can be written as a sum of two different positive integers each at most 100?

[IMC 2014 Q14] This year the Tour de France starts in Leeds on 5 July. Last year, the total length of the Tour was 3404 km and the winner, Chris Froome, took a total time of 83 hours 56 minutes 40 seconds to cover this distance.

Which of these is closest to his average speed over the whole event?

[IMC 2014 Q15] Zac halves a certain number and then adds 8 to the result. He finds that he obtains the same answer if he doubles his original number and then subtracts 8 from the result.

What is Zac’s original number?

Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.

[IMC 2014 Q16] The base of a triangle is increased by 25% but the area of the triangle is unchanged.

By what percentage is the corresponding perpendicular height decreased?
[IMC 2014 Q17] How many weeks are there in [m]8\times7\times6\times5\times4\times3\times2\times1[/m] minutes?

[IMC 2014 Q18] Consider looking from the original [m]\left(0,0\right)[/m] towards all the points [m]\left(m,n\right)[/m], where each of [m]m[/m] and [m]n[/m] is an integer. Some points are hidden, because they are directly in line with another nearer point. For example [m]\left(2,2\right)[/m] is hidden by [m]\left(1,1\right)[/m].

How many of the points [m]\left(6,2\right)[/m],[m]\left(6,3\right)[/m],[m]\left(6,4\right)[/m],[m]\left(6,5\right)[/m] are not hidden points?

subskill.name: Solve problems by use of case analysis.

questions.content:
[IMC 2014 Q19] Suppose that [m]8^m=27[/m].

What is the value of [m]4^m[/m]?

subskill.name: Express a power using a different base.

questions.content:
[IMC 2014 Q20] The diagram shows a regular pentagon and five circular arcs. The sides of the pentagon have length 4. The centre of each arc is a vertex of the pentagon, and the ends of the arc are the midpoints of the two adjacent edges.

What is the total shaded area?

Input note: give your answer in terms of [m]\pi[/m].

subskill.name: Calculate the area of the sector of a circle.

questions.content:
[IMC 2014 Q21] In King Arthur’s jousting tournament, each of the several competing knights receives 17 points for every bout he enters. The winner of each bout receives an extra 3 points. At the end of the tournament, the Black Knight has exactly one more point than the Red Knight.

What is the smallest number of bouts that the Black Knight could have entered?

subskill.name: Determine positive integer solutions to a problem in context that can be modelled as an equation of the form ||ax + by = k||

questions.content:
[IMC 2014 Q22] The positive integers [m]a[/m],[m]b[/m] and [m]c[/m] are all different. None of them is a square but all the products [m]ab[/m],[m]ac[/m] and [m]bc[/m] are squares.

What is the least value that [m]a+b+c[/m] can take?

[IMC 2014 Q23] A sector of a disc is removed by making two straight cuts from the circumference to the centre. The perimeter of the sector has the same length as the circumference of the original disc.

What fraction of the area of the disc is removed?
[IMC 2014 Q24] How many 4-digit integers (from 1000 to 9999) have at least one digit repeated?

[IMC 2014 Q25] The diagram shows two concentric circles with radii 1 and 2 units, together with a shaded octagon, all of whose sides are equal.

What is the length of the perimeter of the octagon?

In the triangle [m]PQR[/m], the point [m]S[/m] is on the edge [m]QR[/m].
[m]\angle QPS=\angle SPR[/m], [m]PQ=PS=SR[/m] and [m]\angle PRQ=x^{\circ}[/m]. 

What is the value of [m]x[/m]?

mathematical statement. Which number should come immediately after the division sign?

In the diagram shown, [m]PQRS[/m] is a rhombus and [m]PQT[/m] is an isosceles triangle in which [m]PT=QT[/m]. Angle [m]PSR=110^{\circ}[/m].
What is the size of angle [m]SQT[/m]?

subskill.name: Determine an angle using multiple angle laws in a diagram that involves a quadrilateral.

[UKMT JMC 2024 Q16]

The world’s smallest vertebrate is much shorter than its name! Discovered in 2022, the frog [m]paedophryne\:amauensis[/m] is only 7.7 mm long.
Approximately how many of these frogs, placed end to end, would be needed to make a line 1 metre long?

subskill.name: Calculate with metric measures of length, which may require conversion.

[UKMT JMC 2024 Q17]

[m]PQRS[/m] is a square with area 100 cm[m]^2[/m].  The point [m]T[/m] is inside the square.
[m]QRT[/m] is a triangle with area 24 cm[m]^2[/m].
What is the area, in cm[m]^2[/m], of the triangle [m]PTS[/m]?

[UKMT JMC 2024 Q18]

Goldilocks eats three equal-sized bowls of porridge, one after the other. When she has eaten [m]\frac{3}{7}[/m] of the total amount of porridge, what fraction of the porridge in the second bowl has she eaten?

subskill.name: Form an expression with one variable and two operations.

questions.content:
[UKMT JMC 2024 Q19]

Jokers always lie.
Clowns always tell the truth.
A group of four, each of whom is a Joker or a Clown, make the following statements about each other:
[m]P[/m] says, “[m]Q[/m] always lies”;
[m]Q[/m] says, “[m]R[/m] always lies”;
[m]R[/m] says, “[m]P[/m] always tells the truth”;
[m]S[/m] says, “Exactly two of [m]P[/m], [m]Q[/m] and [m]R[/m] are Jokers”.

How many of [m]P[/m], [m]Q[/m], [m]R[/m] and [m]S[/m] are Clowns?

[UKMT JMC 2024 Q20]

When you cut a regular hexagon into two pieces with a single straight cut, you get two polygons.
Which of these shapes cannot be obtained?

[UKMT JMC 2024 Q21]

The rectangle [m]PQRS[/m] is divided into eight squares: one large unshaded square, four small unshaded squares and three shaded squares, as shown in the diagram.
What fraction of the area of rectangle [m]PQRS[/m] is shaded?

subskill.name: Form and solve a linear equation for the area of two 2D shapes.

Forty furry ferrets weigh the same as fifty fit ferrets. Forty-five fit ferrets weigh the  same as fifty-four friendly ferrets.
How many friendly ferrets weigh the same as fifty furry ferrets?

subskill.name: Form and solve simultaneous equations/systems of equations with 3 unknown values.

The area of a square is six times the area of a rectangle with a length half that of the square and a width 6 cm less than the width of the square.
What is the perimeter of the square?

subskill.name: Form and solve a linear equation for the area of two 2D shapes.

questions.content:
[UKMT JMC 2024 Q24]

Rovers, United, City and Wanderers played against each other once in a hockey tournament.
The results table is shown below:

Team  Win  Draw  Loss  Goals for  Goals against 
Rovers   3  0  0  5  0
United  0  2  1  3  6
City  1  1  1  4  4
Wanderers   0  1  2  0  2

What was the score in the match between Rovers and United?

[UKMT JMC 2024 Q25]

In a school, one fifth of the students have blue eyes. One tenth of the left-handed students have blue eyes. One quarter of the right-handed students have blue eyes.
What fraction of the students are left-handed?

[JMC 2012 Q5] One of the mascots for the 2012 Olympic Games is called ‘Wenlock’ because the town of Wenlock in Shropshire first held the Wenlock Olympian Games in 1850. How many years ago was that?

(Note, this question was asked in 2012)
[JMC 2012 Q6] The diagrams on the right show three different views of the same cube. Which letters is on the face opposite U?

[JMC 2012 Q7] A small ink cartridge has enough ink to print 600 pages. Three small cartridges can print as many pages as two medium cartridges. Three medium cartridges can print as many pages as two large cartridges.

How many pages can be printed using a large cartridge?

subskill.name: Determine a fraction of an amount given another fraction of that amount.

questions.content: [JMC 2012 Q9] The diagram on the right shows the positions of four people (each marked [m]\times[/m]) in an Art Gallery. In the middle of the room is a stone column. Ali can see none of the other three people. Bea can see only Caz. Caz can see Bea and Dan. Dan can see only Caz. Who is at position [m]P[/m]?

[JMC 2012 Q10] The diagram shows two arrows drawn on separate 4cm × 4cm grids. One arrow points North and the other points West. When the two arrows are drawn on the same 4cm × 4cm grid (still pointing North and West) they overlap.

What is the area of overlap?

[JMC 2012 Q11] In the following expression, each [m]\square[/m] is to be replaced with either + or – in such a way that the result of the calculation is 100.

[m]123\square45\square67\square89[/m]

The number of + signs used is [m]p[/m] and the number of – signs used is [m]m[/m]. What is the value of [m]p-m[/m]?

subskill.name: Determine possible values of variables given some constraints (with algebraic notation).

questions.content: [JMC 2012 Q12] Laura wishes to cut this shape, which is made up of nine small squares, into pieces that she can then rearrange to make a [m]3\times3[/m] square. What is the smallest number of pieces she needs to cut the shape into so that she can do this?

[JMC 2012 Q13] In the multiplication grid on the right, the input factors (in the first row and the first column) are all missing and only some of the products within the table have been given. What is the value of [m]A+B+C+D+E[/m]?

subskill.name: Work out missing numbers in a structure with overlapping lines.

questions.content:
[JMC 2012 Q14] A pattern that repeats every six symbols starts as shown below:

Which are the 100th and 101st symbols, in that order, in the pattern?

[JMC 2012 Q15] Talulah plants 60 tulip bulbs. When they flower, she notes that half are yellow; one third of those which are not yellow are red; and one quarter of those which are neither yellow nor red are pink. The remainder are white.

What fraction of the tulips are white?

[JMC 2012 Q16] Beth, Carolyn and George love reading their favourite bedtime story together. They take it in turns to read a page, always in the order Beth, then Carolyn, then George. All twenty pages of the story are read on each occasion. One evening, Beth is staying at Grandma’s house but Carolyn and George still read the same bedtime story and take it in turns to read a page with Carolyn reading the first page.

In total, how many pages are read by the person who usually reads that page?

[JMC 2012 Q17] There are six more girls than boys in Miss Spelling’s class of 24 pupils. What is the ratio of girls to boys in this class?

Input note: Give your answer as a ratio in simplest form.

subskill.name: Determine a value in a ratio when the difference between two amounts is given.

questions.content: [JMC 2012 Q18] The numbers 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 are to be placed, one per square, in the diagram shown such that the four numbers in the horizontal row add up to 21 and the four numbers in the vertical column also add up to 21. Which number should replace [m]x[/m]?

subskill.name: Work out missing numbers in a structure with overlapping lines.

questions.content: [JMC 2012 Q19] In rectangle [m]PQRS[/m], the ratio of [m]\angle PSQ[/m] to [m]\angle PQS[/m] is [m]1:5[/m]. What is the size of [m]\angle QSR[/m]?
[JMC 2012 Q20] Aroon says his age is 50 years, 50 months, 50 weeks and 50 days old. What age will he be on his next birthday?

[JMC 2012 Q21]

Dominic wants to place the six dominoes above in a hexagonal ring so that, for every pair of adjacent dominoes, the numbers of pips match. The ring on the right indicates how one adjacent pair match. In a completed ring, how many of the other five dominoes can he definitely not place adjacent to  ?

[JMC 2012 Q22] The diagram shows a design formed by drawing six lines in a regular hexagon. The lines divide each edge of the hexagon into three equal parts. What fraction of the hexagon is shaded?

Give your fraction in its simplest form.
[JMC 2012 Q23] Peter wrote a list of all the numbers that could be produced by changing one digit of the number 200. How many of the numbers on Peter’s list are prime?

[JMC 2012 Q24] After playing 500 games, my success rate in Spider Solitaire is 49%. Assuming I win every game from now on, how many extra games do I need to play in order that my success rate increases to 50%?

subskill.name: Calculate the percentage of an amount (less than 100%) using decimal multipliers.

questions.content:

What is the value of [m]x+y[/m]?

Leave your ratio in its simplest form.

options: the ratio depends on the lengths of the sides of the rectangle

subskill.name: Convert metric units of length from smaller units to bigger units.

questions.content:
[JMC 2014 Q15] The diagram shows a rectangular envelope made by folding (and gluing) a single piece of paper. What could the original unfolded piece of paper look like?
(The dashed lines are the fold lines.)

options: C. ‘Statements A to E are true’
D. ‘Statements A to E are false’

questions.content:
[JMC 2014 Q17] The diagram is a ‘map’ of Jo’s local rail network, where the dots represent stations and the lines are routes. Jo wants to visit all the stations, travelling only by train, starting at any station and ending at any station, with no restrictions on which routes are taken.

What is the smallest number of stations that Jo must go to more than once?
[JMC 2014 Q18] Which of these statements is true?

subskill.name: Calculate expressions involving roots and powers using order of operations.

questions.content: [JMC 2014 Q19] Jack and Jill played a game for two people. In each game, the winner was awarded 2 points and the loser 1 point. No games were drawn. Jack won exactly 4 games and Jill had a final score of 10 points. How many games did they play?

[JMC 2014 Q20] Box [m]P[/m] has [m]p[/m] chocolates and box [m]Q[/m] has [m]q[/m] chocolates, where [m]p[/m] and [m]q[/m] are both odd and [m]p > q[/m]. What is the smallest number of chocolates which would have to be moved from [m]P[/m] to box [m]Q[/m] so that box [m]Q[/m] has more chocolates than box P?

[JMC 2014 Q21] Pablo’s teacher has given him 27 identical white cubes. She asks him to paint some of the faces of these cubes grey and then stack the cubes so that they appear as shown. What is the largest possible number of the individual white cubes which Pablo can leave with no faces painted grey?
[JMC 2014 Q22] In the division calculation [m]952473\div18[/m], which two adjacent digits should be swapped in order to increase the result by 100?

[JMC 2014 Q23] Sam wants to complete the diagram so that each of the nine circles contains one of the digits from 1 to 9 inclusive and each contains a different digit. Also, the digits in each of the three lines of four circles must have the same total. What is this total?

subskill.name: Work out missing numbers in a structure with overlapping lines.

questions.content: [JMC 2014 Q24] The diagram shows a regular octagon with sides of length 1. The octagon is divided into regions by four diagonals. What is the difference between the area of the hatched region and the area of the region shaded grey?

[JMC 2014 Q25] A die has the shape of a regular tetrahedron, with the four faces having 1, 2 3 and 4 pips. The die is placed with 4 pips ‘face down’ in one corner of the triangular grid shown, so that the face with 4 pips precisely covers the triangle marked with 4 pips.

The die is now ‘rolled’ by rotating around an edge without slipping, so that 1 pip is face down. It is rolled again, so that 2 pips are face down, as indicated. The rolling continues until the die rests on the shaded triangle in the opposite corner of the grid.

How many pips are now face down?

options: it depends on the route taken

Knave of Hearts: "I stole the tarts."
Knave of Clubs: "The Knave of Hearts is lying."
Knave of Diamonds: "The Knave of Clubs is lying."
Knave of Spades: "The Knave of Diamonds is lying."

How far should Gill place the centre of each of the two remaining pictures from a vertical line down the centre of the wall?

What fraction of the area of the hexagon is shaded? Give your fraction in its simplest form.

What is the area of the region where squares overlap (shown dark grey)?

[JMC 2015 Q24] A palindromic number is a number that reads the same when the order of its digits is reversed.

What is the difference between the largest and smallest five-digit palindromic numbers that are both multiples of 45?

Exam Practice: Solve multiplication, addition and subtraction problems involving missing digits.

questions.content: [JMC 2013 Q1] Which of the following has the largest value?

subskill.name: Solve problems by use of case analysis.

questions.content: [JMC 2013 Q2] Heidi is 2.1m tall, while Lola is only 1.4m tall. What is their average (mean) height?

subskill.name: Calculate the mean of listed data.

questions.content: [JMC 2013 Q3] What is the value of [m]x[/m]?
[JMC 2013 Q4] Gill went for a five-hour walk. Her average speed was between 3 km/h and 4 km/h. Which of the following could be the distance she walked?
[JMC 2013 Q5] The diagram shows a weaver’s design for a rihlélo, a winnowing tray from Mozambique. How many lines of symmetry does the design have?

subskill.name: Identify lines of symmetry in 2D shapes.

questions.content:
[JMC 2013 Q6] What is the value of:

[m]\left(\left(1-1\right)-1\right)-\left(1-\left(1-1\right)\right)[/m]

subskill.name: Add and subtract more than two positive and negative numbers.

questions.content:
[JMC 2013 Q7] After tennis training, Andy collects twice as many balls as Roger and five more than Maria.

They collect 35 balls in total. How many balls does Andy collect?

subskill.name: Form and solve a linear equation involving a relationship between two or more items.

questions.content:
[JMC 2013 Q8] Two identical rulers are placed together, as shown (not to scale). Each ruler is exactly 10cm long and is marked in centimetres from 0 to 10. The 3cm mark on each ruler is aligned with the 4cm mark on the other.

The overall length is L cm. What is the value of L?
[JMC 2013 Q9] Peter has three times as many sisters as brothers. His sister Louise has twice as many sisters as brothers. How many children are there in the family?

subskill.name: Form and solve linear simultaneous equations/systems of equations for a given non-geometric context.

questions.content:
[JMC 2013 Q10] On standard dice the total number of pips on each pair of opposite faces is 7. Two standard dice are placed in a stack, as shown, so that the total number of pips on the two touching faces is 5.

What is the total number of pips on the top and bottom faces of the stack?

[JMC 2013 Q11] Usain runs twice as fast as his mum. His mum runs five times as fast as his pet tortoise, Turbo. They all set off together for a run down the same straight path.

When Usain has run 100m, how far apart are his mum and Turbo the tortoise?
[JMC 2013 Q12] How many hexagons are there in the diagram?

[JMC 2013 Q13] When painting the lounge, I used half of a 3 litre can to complete the first coat of paint. I then used two thirds of what was left to complete the second coat.

How much paint was left after both coats were complete?

subskill.name: Determine an amount after a fractional decrease.

questions.content: [JMC 2013 Q14] Each side of an isosceles triangle is a whole number of centimetres. Its perimeter has length 20cm. How many possibilities are there for the lengths of its sides?

subskill.name: Use the triangle inequality to reason about the lengths of sides of a triangle.

questions.content:
[JMC 2013 Q15] The Grand Old Duke of York had 10 000 men. He lost 10% of them on way to the top of the hill, and he lost 15% of the rest as he marched them back down the hill.

What percentage of the 10 000 men were still there when they reached the bottom of the hill?

subskill.name: Solve problems in context involving percentage changes and arithmetic operations, without a calculator.

questions.content:
[JMC 2013 Q16] Ulysses, Kim, Mei and Tanika have their 12th, 14th, 15th and 15th birthdays on the same day in 2013.

In what year will their ages total 100?

[JMC 2013 Q17] A 5cm [m]\times[/m] 5cm square is cut into five pieces, as shown. Each cut is a sequence of identical copies of the same shape but pointing up, down, left or right. Which piece has the longest perimeter?

[JMC 2013 Q18] Weighing the baby at the clinic was a problem. The baby would not keep still and caused the scales to wobble. So I held the baby and stood on the scales while the nurse read off 78kg.

Then the nurse held the baby while I read off 69kg. Finally I held the nurse while the baby read off 137kg.

What was the combined weight of all three?

subskill.name: Form and solve simultaneous equations/systems of equations with 3 unknown values.

questions.content:
[JMC 2013 Q19] A swimming club has three categories of members: junior, senior, veteran. The ratio of junior to senior members is [m]3:2[/m] and the ratio of senior members to veterans is [m]5:2[/m].

Which of the following could be the total number of members in the swimming club?

subskill.name: Combine ratios in order to reflect on the total possible quantity of items.

questions.content:
[JMC 2013 Q20] A ‘long knight’ moves on a square grid.

A single move, as shown, consists of moving three squares in one direction (horizontally or vertically) and then one square at right angles to the first direction.

What is the smallest number of moves a long knight requires to go from one corner of a [m]8\times8[/m] square board to the diagonally opposite corner?

[JMC 2013 Q21] The [m]5\times4[/m] grid is divided into blocks. Each block is a square or a rectangle and contains the number of cells indicated by the integer within it. Which integer will be in the same block as the shaded cell?

[JMC 2013 Q22] Two numbers in the [m]4\times4[/m] grid can be swapped to create a Magic Square (in which all rows, all columns and both main diagonals add to the same total).

What is the sum of these two numbers?

subskill.name: Work out missing numbers in a structure with overlapping lines.

questions.content:
[JMC 2013 Q23] In our school netball league a team gains a certain whole number of points if it wins a game, a lower whole number of points if it draws a game and no points if it loses a game.

After 10 games my team has won 7 games, drawn 3 and gained 44 points. My sister’s team has won 5 games, drawn 2 and lost 3.

How many points has her team gained?

subskill.name: Determine possible values of variables given a relationship (with algebraic notation).

questions.content:
[JMC 2013 Q24] Three congruent squares overlap as shown. The areas of the three overlapping sections are 2 cm2, 5 cm2 and 8 cm2 respectively. The total area of the non-overlapping parts of the squares is 117 cm2.

What is the side-length of each square?

[JMC 2013 Q25] For Beatrix’s latest art installation, she has fixed a [m]2\times2[/m] square sheet of steel to a wall.

She has two [m]1\times2[/m] magnetic tiles, both which she attaches to the steel sheet, in any orientation, so that none of the sheet is visible and the line separating the two tiles cannot be seen. As shown alongside, one tile has one black cell and one grey cell; the other tile has one black cell and one spotted cell.

How many different looking [m]2\times2[/m] installations can Beatrix obtain?
